abstract: Accurate prediction of mutation-induced changes in protein-protein binding free energy (ΔΔG) remains limited by small, redundant datasets and train-test homology leakage. We show that commonly used SKEMPI2 splits inflate model performance, with every tested AI predictor declining under a stringent split that controls homology at the level of individual chains (60% sequence identity). We introduce ProtBFF, a modular framework that integrates five residue-level biophysical descriptors into pretrained protein representations through cross-embedding attention. Under leakage-controlled evaluation, ProtBFF improves performance across five sequence- and structure-based encoders. ESM-C achieves the highest Pearson correlation (0.469), while SaProt achieves the highest Spearman correlation (0.437), surpassing specialized ΔΔG predictors. Ablations identify interface features as the dominant contribution and show that pretrained embeddings and biophysical features provide complementary information. ProtBFF also improves low-data transfer to SARS-CoV-2 binding datasets, demonstrating the value of explicit biophysical priors for robust ΔΔG prediction.
